content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing a problem with a [product_name] [article_no] module. The device powers up as expected, but attempting to download a program triggers an error (see attachment). My connection to the device is through Ethernet only. Can anyone suggest what might be causing this? Regards, [user_name]

When you transfer your program from the computer to the [product_name] the computer first performs a checksum. The checksum is then sent to the [product_name] along with your program. The device verifies the checksum and compares it to the transmitted value. If they match, the program is enabled for use. If not, the program won't be activated and your computer will receive a message. Possible reasons include a poor connection or faulty connector. Try reinserting the connectors on both the computer and device. If the issue persists, slightly change your program (such as adding a marker) and attempt the transfer again. Good luck.

Which version of [product_name] software are you using? There was a BIOS update between [version_no] and [version_no] that affects checksum verification during transfers. I recommend checking your cable, as communication is crucial for successful checksum exchange. Also, if you're switching between ladder and function block programs, try converting the program before uploading/downloading.

Thank you for your suggestions. I'm using [product_name] software [version_no]. I can successfully download to another [product_name] [article_no] unit, but not to the [article_no]. It's possible my [article_no] unit is faulty. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], please also check the following: 1. What details are shown when you click the information icon? (see attached image). 2. Which hardware type did you select when downloading to the [product_name] [article_no]? (see attached image). Greetings, [user_name]

Thank you all for your advice. I accidentally created a program using Q8 as an output, and this one downloaded successfully (no expansion modules attached). When I try downloading a program without Q8, I get a checksum error. Hope this helps someone else. Regards, [user_name]

With [product_name] software, you can use inputs and outputs in your program that aren't present on your [product_name]—for example, I9...I24 or Q9...Q16—these are available on expansion units. Even without expansion units, you can transfer the program. Note that data for expansion units is only operational when the device is in RUN mode—not during transfer. You may use outputs like Q9..Q16 as markers in your program if desired. The program will work, but these outputs will only operate in software, not hardware. Therefore, a program with Q8 typically won't cause a checksum error. If possible, please share your program for review. Have you pressed F2? This can also reveal possible errors (ensure View > Info Window is enabled).

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members discuss troubleshooting a checksum error when transferring programs to a [product_name] [article_no] module using Ethernet. The main topics include potential hardware communication faults, software version compatibility, and use of specific outputs in project configuration. The issue was resolved when the user included an output (Q8), enabling successful download, which suggests that program structure can directly influence checksum validation on this hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects program transfers to work reliably and consistently, without facing checksum errors, regardless of output selection or program configuration.
